title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
hook: Meta released Llama 2 with open weights and a commercial-use license, giving anyone a strong RLHF-tuned chat model to build on - and kicked off a wave of open-LLM development.
key_points: Releases both base and chat-tuned variants (7B to 70B), with RLHF and rejection sampling used to align the chat models.
Permissive license allowed commercial use, which accelerated community fine-tuning and the open-LLM ecosystem.
Used two separate reward models - one for helpfulness, one for safety - and iterative RLHF to balance both.
Llama 2-Chat outperformed most open models at the time on human preference evaluations.
content_html: Meta's Touvron and colleagues released Llama 2 in July 2023, providing pretrained base models and instruction-tuned chat variants ranging from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters. Unlike many frontier releases, the weights were made publicly available under a license that permitted commercial use, which set it apart from its predecessor and from most contemporaries.
extra_html:
How it works

The base models were trained on roughly 2 trillion tokens of public data. The chat variants went through supervised fine-tuning on human-annotated conversations, then iterative reinforcement learning from human feedback using two reward models — one optimizing for helpfulness, one for safety — to navigate the tension between the two goals.

Why it matters

Open weights with a permissive license meant researchers and companies could fine-tune, quantize, and deploy Llama 2 without restriction, catalyzing a wave of community models (instruction tunes, merges, distillations) that would not have been possible with closed-weights releases. The careful dual-reward RLHF approach also became a reference point for open alignment work. Read the full paper on arXiv.

related.title: LLaMA: Open & Efficient Foundation Models
related.hook: You don't need a 175B-parameter model to compete. LLaMA trained smaller models on lots of public data — and lit a fire under the open-weights community.

related.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
related.hook: Meta's Llama 3 family, trained on roughly 15 trillion tokens with a 405B-parameter flagship, narrowed the gap to closed frontier models while staying open-weights.

related.title: InstructGPT: Aligning LMs with Human Feedback (RLHF)
related.hook: A smaller model people actually like beats a bigger one they don't. InstructGPT used human preferences to make a model follow instructions — the recipe behind ChatGPT.

flashcards.back_html: One optimized for helpfulness and one for safety, to navigate the tension between the two goals via iterative RLHF.

flashcards.prompt: Why did Llama 2's permissive license matter for the ecosystem?

choices.text: It allowed commercial use, accelerating community fine-tuning and open-LLM development
It restricted the model to academic research only
It required users to share their training data with Meta

flashcards.explanation_html: Open weights plus a commercial-use license let researchers and companies fine-tune, quantize, and deploy freely.
